title: Why a geometric series cancels itself
subtitle: Geometric Series · Grade 10

beats.narration: Can we add one, two, four, and eight without counting every number? There is a beautiful shortcut hiding in the pattern.
Notice what happens from one term to the next. We multiply by two, again and again. Two is called the common ratio.
Let us call the whole sum S. So S equals one plus two plus four plus eight. We will find S using a clever subtraction.
Double every term, not just the first one. Two S equals two plus four plus eight plus sixteen. Watch how the numbers line up.
Put the doubled sum above the original sum. The two, four, and eight now sit in the same columns. Those are the terms that will disappear.
Subtract the original S from two S. The matching middle terms cancel each other. We are left with sixteen minus one. And two S minus S is just S, so S equals fifteen.

This trick works for any geometric progression. Multiply the sum by the common ratio r, then subtract. The sum of n terms equals a times the bracket r to the power n minus one, all divided by r minus one. Remember, r cannot equal one here.
Now try one yourself. Add one, three, nine, and twenty-seven. If you multiply this sum by three, which terms will cancel? Pause the video and work it out on paper.

Three S equals three plus nine plus twenty-seven plus eighty-one. Subtract S and the matching terms disappear. Two S equals eighty-one minus one, which is eighty. Therefore S equals forty. You have discovered the geometric series shortcut.
